Definition: a thong (as compressing); by analogy, a tendon
BiblicalUsage: gîyd is the word for a sinew, a tendon. In Genesis 32:32, the text says "Therefore the children of Israel eat not [of] the sinew which shrank." In Job 10:11, the text says "and hast fenced me with bones and sinews."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading gîyd this way, I believe strength is not something we muster; it is something God gives to the weak. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Jacob Wrestles with God; The Valley of Dry Bones
